title: Кольцо в пирожном под ответственность Шефа  (The Ring in the Pastry Under the Chef's Responsibility)

segments.t: Wanting the proposal to be truly romantic, Vika suggests hiding the diamond ring inside Kristina's favorite dessert pastry. Nagiyev loves the idea and places the ring directly under Chef Barinov's personal responsibility, warning him that the ring cost a fortune on credit.
Вы же помните, как она пирожное любила?
Мы положим кольцо ей в пирожное.
Во-первых, оно дорогое, во-вторых, оно еще в кредит...
Now let's break down each line of their conversation.
'I have an idea.' Vika steps in evenly in their talk, without trying to dress up how she really feels.
'Get out of here.' Nagiyev counters vividly on the spot and reaches for the Russian word "otsyuda" ("from here") right at the heart of the line.

'We should put the ring inside a pastry.' Dwelling on the pastries during the talk, Vika leans on "nado" ("it is necessary, one needs to"), which carries the whole predicate in Russian without needing "it is".
Вы же помните, как она пирожное любила?
'You remember how much she loved that pastry, right?' Nagiyev prompts straight out whether Vika really thought this through.
Мы положим кольцо ей в пирожное.
'We will hide the ring inside her pastry.' Highlighting the pastries beside Nagiyev, Vika reaches for the Russian word "pirozhnoye" ("pastries, cakes") right at the heart of the line.
'That is an excellent idea.' Emphasizing how excellent things are on the spot, Nagiyev links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'Not Vika—Vitya.' Nagiyev steps in pointedly without holding back, to clear the air between them once and for all.
'The ring is under your personal responsibility.' Touching on the responsibility during the talk, Nagiyev puts the emphasis on "otvetstvennost" ("responsibility") in the middle of the talk.
'I beg you, be very careful with it.' Vika pushes back evenly with a nod, letting the remark speak for itself.
Во-первых, оно дорогое, во-вторых, оно еще в кредит...
'First of all, it is expensive, and second, I bought it on credit...' Nagiyev jumps in plainly in their talk, letting the remark speak for itself.
'Do not worry about it.' Vika responds calmly with Nagiyev and centers the thought on "volnuysya" ("worry", from "volnovatsya") without wasting a word.
'Everything will be fine.' Focusing on the order right here, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 4 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'How are things going with you?' Vika wonders briskly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
Вы же помните, как она пирожное любила?
Мы положим кольцо ей в пирожное.
Во-первых, оно дорогое, во-вторых, оно еще в кредит...
That wraps up this scene as vika suggests hiding the engagement ring inside Kristina's favorite pastry, and Nagiyev entrusts the expensive ring to Chef Barinov until dessert. Until next time!
